title: Role workspace (knowledge/_roles/<module>/<lane>.yaml)
description: One lane's place in the shared knowledge base (T99/T103). A lane is BA, SA or DEV — the three columns of V1.5's diagram — and this file holds only the two things that are lane-local and cannot be derived: the watermark of what the person in that lane has acknowledged, and that person's sign-off on the lane's own output. Everything else a caller might want (what the lane is working on, what changed under it, whether it is waiting on somebody) is computed from knowledge/ every time it is asked, because a stored copy of a derivation is a second source of truth waiting to disagree with the first — and, for a notification list specifically, one that keeps escalating things somebody already fixed (T66's lesson).

lane.description: Which of V1.5's columns this is. Derived from T67's ViewName, not a fourth vocabulary: ba=business, sa=architecture, dev=technical, uxui=design authority (T145).

module.description: The module folder this lane's work belongs to, or null for project-wide. Mirrors a knowledge item's own `module`, and decides the directory the same way: null lives under _project/.

seen.description: The watermark: which version of which item the person in this lane has acknowledged. This is the whole input to change propagation — an item that moved past its entry here is what T105/T106 report. It advances by an explicit human acknowledgement and by nothing else: if merely retrieving an item advanced it, every notification would be marked read before anyone saw it.

signoffs.description: This lane's own approval gate (T103), oldest first, last one wins. Only a person writes one — `knowledge/_roles/**` is denied to every agent at the tool level. There is no `pending` status on purpose: 'asked but unanswered' is the derived stage `awaiting-signoff`, and storing it as well would be a second copy free to disagree. A sign-off records the exact item versions it covers, so amending one of them makes it stale automatically rather than leaving a flag that outlives the thing it approved.

type.description: Which of CLAUDE.md's five always-human points this lane's gate is. Reused from the T08 ledger's ApprovalType rather than a parallel vocabulary.

items.description: Exactly what was signed off, at the versions it was signed off at.

note.description: What they said beyond yes/no. The reason a rejection is actionable rather than just a stop.

id.description: A knowledge item id — the same id space as knowledge-item.schema.json, not a parallel one.

version.description: The item's version at the moment it was acknowledged. Never a version the item has not reached: staleReferences() calls that `ahead`, which means the two are not talking about the same item.

by.description: The person who acknowledged it. Free text, like an approval's decidedBy — this pipeline has no identity system and pretending otherwise would be worse. Required and non-empty because an acknowledgement with nobody attached is the exact thing V1.5 forbids: an agent marking work seen on a human's behalf.
